headline: Nor’easter leaves more than 100,000 without power as storm lingers
dek: The slow-moving storm has caused a fatal falling-tree incident in Brooklyn and widespread outages while rain, coastal flooding and localized street flooding remain possible into Monday.
body: A slow-moving nor’easter continued to affect the Northeast on Sunday, with more than 100,000 customers without power across the region and mid-Atlantic, according to Associated Press reporting that cited PowerOutage.us. The storm was expected to linger near the coast before gradually weakening.

The storm also turned deadly in New York City. A 56-year-old New York City Housing Authority employee died after a falling tree struck him in Brooklyn on Saturday, according to the Associated Press and New York City storm reports. The incident came as saturated ground and strong winds increased the risk of falling trees and limbs.

In southern New England, the National Weather Service Boston/Norton office says windswept rain, minor coastal flooding and beach erosion remain possible, along with localized urban and street flooding, through Monday. Some coastal wind warnings have eased, but repeated downpours can still overwhelm drainage and low-lying roads.

Residents should monitor the latest local alerts, avoid driving through water covering a roadway and use caution near the coast. Outage and travel conditions may change quickly as the low shifts and communities clear downed trees, wires and debris.
author: NorthEast News Desk
sourceName: Associated Press; National Weather Service Boston/Norton
